Describe your solution (100 -200): At Kuphila AI, we develop machine learning algorithms to perform diagnostics on medical images and pathology slides. We utilize Edge-AI technology to ensure that these algorithms run on mobile devices without requiring continuous Internet access. The cervi-detect solution can analyze pap smear images and determine if the sample under view contains characteristics of a cancerous cell or not.
What healthcare problem does your soluti: A severe lack of pathologists that leads to a backlog in diagnosis and treatment. In cases like cervical cancer, the diagnostic problem implies that when the laboratory test results come back manually, it means that the disease is usually advanced.
What will you demo at the AI in Health S:
Kuphila AI will showcase a real full end-to-end simulation of our Edge-Native digital specialist application running within a real-world, low-resource environment.

The demo will be done on a normal, mid-range Android cell phone in full Airplane Mode, as this will really demonstrate our unique selling proposition, our ability to work 100% Offline.

The live demonstration will go through the following process:

Offline Image Capture: A high-resolution cervical cancer pathology slide/medical image will be uploaded to the mobile device as if it were from the front line of healthcare, where a nurse would take a sample and upload it to a primary healthcare center in the rural area.

On-Device Edge Inference: The crowd will be able to see our machine learning model, which uses 4-bit/8-bit quantization, to analyze the medical image locally on the phone's built-in processor, without requiring internet connectivity or cloud dependency.

Real-time diagnostic output: The application will immediately provide the user with a computer vision heatmap to mark abnormal areas in the cells and an automatic diagnostic risk report, with the heatmap localized in the region of the image.

In this demo, we will demonstrate that sophisticated cancer screening does not need a multi-million dollar laboratory infrastructure or the need for high-speed internet—thereby moving life-saving cancer detection to the point of care, where the specialist lives and works.
Why do you want to participate in the Sh: To prove our offline AI to B2B/B2G buyers, secure clinical pilots, and attract health-tech VCs.
What makes your solution innovative or u:
The key thing that makes Kuphila AI unique is that we're not just creating diagnostic software; we've completely separated high-tech medical imagery from the infrastructure needs.

Many traditional medical AI platforms need to use a considerable amount of cloud computing to analyze dense and high-resolution pathology slides, which are often too large to fit hospital networks. Our models are optimized for local use, without a requirement for a stable internet connection, so screening for cancer can go beyond the central urban laboratory and directly into the off-grid, rural laboratory.

Sofisticated neural networks compressed to 4-bit and 8-bit: We managed to quantize sophisticated neural networks successfully to 4 bit and 8 bit. This means that our algorithms are not so dependent on high-end specialized hardware and instead run directly on the mid-tier mobile devices that frontline health workers already carry – comparable to the processing power of high-end lab equipment.

Hyper-Localized Optimization: Most of the global medical algorithms are trained using the majority of the Western demographic datasets. We develop our models using data that specifically captures the biological diversity in Africa, and they are customized to fit into existing workflow constraints with minimal operational friction in clinics throughout the region.

Its easy Pay-Per-Scan revenue model drives the elimination of massive start-up costs for tiny clinics, making it a real force multiplier to reduce the diagnostic backlog.

The Bottom Line: We're building a regular mobile phone to be an off-line special level pathology lab—empowering the underserved populace to get life savers early screening for cancer in weeks rather than months.

The Core Problem: A Fragmented, Paper-Based, and Disconnected Healthcare System
Nigeria's healthcare system serves approximately 230 million people across 36 states, yet it operates without a unified patient records infrastructure. Despite being Africa's most populous nation and largest economy, EHR adoption in Nigeria stands at a critically low 18%, compared to over 90% in the United States. The consequences of this gap are severe and far-reaching.
Problem Dimension
Reality on the Ground
Fragmented patient records
Patient records almost never follow a patient from one facility to another — private clinics, public hospitals, and labs operate in complete data silos

No national patient identity

Infrastructure barriers

Nigeria carries 26% of the global malaria burden, has 2.4 million people living with HIV, and faces a rapidly rising tide of non-communicable diseases such as hypertension (affecting 28–32% of adults) and diabetes — all while operating with a doctor-to-patient ratio of roughly 1:9,000. The Problem We Are Solving

Africa is home to some of the most resilient, resourceful, and community-rooted people on earth. Yet across the continent, and most acutely in Nigeria, access to quality healthcare remains one of the most persistent and consequential inequalities of our time.

The numbers are not abstract. They are people.

One doctor for every five thousand Nigerians in urban areas. One for every forty thousand in rural communities. Over fifteen thousand trained Nigerian doctors lost to emigration between 2020 and 2023 alone. Clinics overwhelmed. Waiting times measured in days. Health records scattered across paper forms or lost entirely. And an unregulated medicine market in which the World Health Organisation estimates that up to forty-two percent of medicines circulating in sub-Saharan Africa are fake, substandard, or dangerously adulterated — meaning that a patient who makes the journey to find medicine may return home with something that does nothing, or worse, causes active harm.

For most Nigerians, navigating this system means making critical health decisions with incomplete information, inadequate access, and no reliable way to know who or what to trust.

This is the problem NaptiQ-Care was built to solve.

What Healthcare Problem Does Our Solution Address?

NaptiQ-Care addresses five interconnected healthcare problems that together constitute the most significant barrier to health equity in Nigeria and across sub-Saharan Africa. These are not separate challenges. They are five faces of the same crisis — a system that was never built to serve everyone, leaving the majority of the population to navigate illness, uncertainty, and risk without the tools, information, or access they need.

Problem One — The Doctor Shortage Crisis

Nigeria has a doctor-to-patient ratio of approximately one physician per five thousand people in urban areas, and as low as one per forty thousand in rural communities. 
Between 2020 and 2023 alone, Nigeria lost over fifteen thousand trained doctors to emigration — to the United Kingdom, Canada, the United States, and other destinations offering better pay, safer working conditions, and more functional health systems. 

Clinics are overwhelmed. Waiting times stretch across entire days. Rural health posts operate without qualified staff for weeks at a time. The result is that millions of Nigerians make their most consequential health decisions — whether to seek care, what symptoms to monitor, when something is serious — without access to any qualified guidance whatsoever.

NaptiQ-Care's AI pre-diagnostic tool does not replace a doctor. Nothing can or should. But it closes the most dangerous gap in this crisis

Problem Two — The Fake Medicine Crisis

The World Health Organisation estimates that up to forty-two percent of medicines circulating in sub-Saharan Africa are fake, substandard, or dangerously adulterated. This is not a peripheral problem. It is a mass public health emergency that operates largely in plain sight.

The people buying these products are not making reckless choices. They are making the only choice available to them. They do not know which pharmacy is registered and which is not. They do not have a map of verified healthcare providers. They go where it is closest and cheapest because they have no tool that tells them anything different.

NaptiQ-Care's live facility map directly solves this problem. Every pharmacy listed on the platform is registered and verified. For the first time, any Nigerian anywhere in the country can open an app, see exactly which pharmacies near them are legitimate, and walk through the right door with confidence. 

Problem Three — The Health Information Gap

Most Nigerians make health decisions without adequate information. This is not a failure of intelligence or education. It is a failure of access.

When a child has a fever at midnight in a village two hours from the nearest clinic, a parent needs to know whether this is something they can manage at home through the night or whether they need to begin the journey immediately. When an elderly man notices his blood pressure readings have been creeping upward over the past three weeks, he needs to know whether this is a pattern worth discussing urgently with a doctor or a normal fluctuation. When a market woman buys medicine from a stall because it is what she can afford and what is available, she deserves to know whether what she is taking is real.

These are not questions that require a medical degree to answer. They require access to reliable, contextual, plain-language health guidance — the kind of guidance that people with private doctors, educated family members, or high-quality internet access take entirely for granted. NaptiQ-Care democratises that access.

roblem Four — The Invisible Health History

One of the most consistently underestimated problems in Nigerian healthcare is the absence of patient health records at the point of care.

A patient arriving at a clinic they have never visited before arrives as a complete unknown. No medication history. No previous diagnoses. No record of allergies, chronic conditions, or prior treatments. The consultation begins from zero.
